azure.note: Separate infra plane, not part of the on-prem vSphere/ExportList.csv inventory above. Sourced from Analisis Azure.docx (internal, treat with the same 'grain of salt' caveat as other Relevamiento-derived material) and Arquitectura_Configuraciones_Instalacion.docx. Condor Work/Enterprise/ProvIA application tiers run here, not on the vSphere VMs.

s2s_vpn_to_onprem.traffic: very low, mostly OnPrem->Azure (Oracle DB access, point integrations)

s2s_vpn_to_onprem.route: 10.77.0.0/16 routed to on-prem datacenter via VPN gateway

security_findings: No Network Security Groups (NSG) in either prod or devtest VNet.
No Azure Firewall, no Private Endpoints identified.

Both prod and devtest use a single flat subnet shared by app traffic, VPN, and internet-facing services — no internal segmentation. A compromise inside the AKS cluster could move laterally without restriction.

core_vm.note: Standalone Azure VM (explicitly 'una Virtual Machine de Azure' per arquitectura_configuraciones_instalacion.txt, NOT a container in AKS). Not present in ExportList.csv (not a vSphere VM) and not previously captured in this azure section. Resolves the B2C user -> org -> ORDS endpoint mapping; central to login for Work/Enterprise/ProvIA.
core_vm.priority: high — likely a single point of failure for login across multiple products/clients
